title: CLO 2026.0 - Virtual Model
description: CLO 2026.0 version has been officially released — Make it, for real! In the new version, the virtual model feature has been further optimized, allowing you to modify and create virtual models more quickly.
transcript:
In this update of version 2026.0, the functions related to virtual models have been enhanced, making it easier and more convenient to modify and create virtual models, including the new hybrid transformation feature. Let’s take a closer look at these functions.

First of all, the hybrid transformation function allows you to freely adjust the body and facial expressions of virtual models using hybrid transformation data within the software.

Hybrid transformation refers to data created in external 3D tools, which includes various body shapes and facial transformation values beyond the default form.

Starting with this version, when you import the data into the software, you only need to move the slider to see the changes in real time.

Currently, we support GLB/GLTF and VRM formats.

Future plans include expanding support to more formats.

Let me show you the hybrid transformation function and how to change the body shape of the virtual model.

I have added a virtual model containing various body data and loaded it.

In the main menu, select the virtual model and open the virtual model editor.

Then select the hybrid transformation tab from the label bar.

In the variable parameter list, you will see the adjustable shape keys.

If you move the slider, you can see the virtual model’s body shape change in real time.

Open the simulation.

The clothing will also shrink simultaneously as the model’s body shape changes.

The hybrid transformation function supports a variety of modifications.

Specifically, it depends on the data type contained in the base virtual model.

This time, let’s add a virtual model file containing facial expression data.

Select import from the main menu, then choose GLTF.

Select the file to save as a virtual model.

Check the variable parameter list.

You will find that this virtual model includes more hybrid transformations than the previous model.

It also has many different adjustable parts.

You can collapse the data folders for each different area.

Because the facial expression data is pre-made in the external tool,

you can adjust the slider

to observe extremely subtle changes in the virtual model’s expression.

Click on the star icon.

You can set your commonly used items as collections.

By turning on the high-resolution collection in the upper right corner,

you can focus more on adjusting the necessary items.

Click on all items again.

If you want to restore all values to their original state at once,

just click the reset button.

Next, let’s look at the customized configuration process after the improvement.

Now you can store external documents containing binding information

as ZACS documents together with virtual models.

The key is that the name of the joint set in the configuration

must be the same as the name of the virtual model

that needs to be merged with the virtual model.

Check the name of the virtual model’s joint points.

Select the virtual model in the main menu.

Select the customized configuration and open the window.

I will add a hair file here.

Add the prepared file.

You will find that the name of the joint in the configuration hair

matches the name of the virtual model joint.

Therefore, no additional steps are required to merge it immediately with the virtual model.

Select bind in the basic part.

In the customized configuration window,

set the ratio and shrink chart to automatic.

Then you can save it directly as a virtual model configuration file.

The saved file will be created in the ZACS file format.

This is the custom configuration format for CLO.

You can easily use this method

to customize both external virtual models and CLO virtual models.

We have also added a type of cartoon effect that can make your clothes and virtual models look like 2D cartoons.

Double-click the virtual model to select it.

Then, in the material options tab of the property editor,

change the type to “Cartoon Effect Only 3D.”

The selected virtual model and configuration will be converted to a 2D cartoon style.

Once the cartoon material type is switched,

a detailed effect option will appear at the bottom.

Let’s take a quick look.

In the shadow section, you can choose the shadow color.

Increasing the strength will make the edge of the shadow sharper,

and adjusting the flatness can change the range of the shadow.

Let’s adjust the parameters to check the effect.

Finally, select a mode in the contour line section,

and adjust the width value.

You can create contour lines,

and generate high-quality cartoon textures.

For more detailed options on the cartoon effect material type,

please visit the CLO official website.

Finally, starting from this version,

we support UV editing for CLO virtual models and external virtual models.

From the main menu, start the UV editor,

then select the UV editor.

In the vertical menu bar,

you can add UV display objects.

You can selectively check the UV maps

of the virtual model

or the costume in the 3D window at the moment,

and display the UVs.

Open the virtual model display.

You can see all the UV maps

of the virtual model in the interface.

If you only want to check the map of the selected object,

select the UV display object in the display objects,

and only display this map in the interface.

In this way, even if the screen content is very complex,

you can select and place only the required elements,

thereby greatly simplifying the workflow.

The above covers the various improvements of virtual models in CLO,

from hybrid transformation to the fun cartoon effect material.

We hope these new features will make your work easier and more pleasant.

Thank you for watching.

chunks.content: # CLO 2026.0 - Virtual Model Enhancements This document details the new and improved features related to virtual models in CLO version 2026.0, including hybrid transformation, customized configuration, cartoon effect materials, and UV editing support for both CLO and external virtual models. --- ## Hybrid Transformation Function for Virtual Models This section explains the hybrid transformation feature, which enables real-time adjustment of virtual model body shapes and facial expressions using externally created transformation data. - **Definition:** Hybrid transformation involves data created in external 3D tools that includes various body shapes and facial transformation values beyond the default virtual model. - **Supported Formats:** GLB/GLTF and VRM formats are currently supported, with plans to expand supported formats in future updates. - **Usage:** - Import a virtual model containing hybrid transformation data. - Open the Virtual Model Editor from the main menu and select the "Hybrid Transformation" tab. - Adjust shape keys via sliders to see real-time changes in body shape and facial expressions. - Clothing automatically shrinks or expands in sync with body shape changes. - **Facial Expression Adjustments:** - Import virtual models with facial expression data using GLTF format. - Variable parameter lists show multiple adjustable parts for subtle expression changes. - Users can collapse data folders by area for easier navigation. - **Favorites & Collections:** - Use the star icon to mark commonly used sliders as collections. - Activate the high-resolution collection to focus on detailed adjustments. - **Reset Function:** - A reset button restores all adjustable parameters to their original default values. --- ## Customized Configuration and ZACS Document Integration This section covers improvements to the customized configuration process, allowing seamless merging of external documents with virtual models. - **ZACS Document Support:** External files containing binding information can be saved as ZACS documents alongside virtual models. - **Joint Name Matching:** The joint set names in the configuration file must match the virtual model’s joint names to enable automatic merging. - **Procedure:** - Verify the joint names of the virtual model. - Open the customized configuration window from the main menu. - Add external files such as hair models with matching joint names. - Select “bind” in the basic settings. - Set the ratio and shrink chart to automatic. - Save the configuration as a ZACS file, CLO’s custom configuration format. - **Benefits:** This method facilitates easy customization of both CLO native and external virtual models without additional manual steps. --- ## Cartoon Effect Material for 2D Style Rendering This section describes the newly added cartoon effect material type that converts 3D virtual models and their clothing into 2D cartoon-style visuals. - **Activation:** - Double-click the virtual model to select it. - In the Property Editor, open the Material Options tab. - Change the material type to “Cartoon Effect Only 3D.” - **Effect Options:** - **Shadow Section:** - Choose shadow color. - Adjust shadow strength to sharpen edges. - Modify flatness to control shadow range. - **Contour Line Section:** - Select contour line mode.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Virtual Model
chunks.content: --- ## Cartoon Effect Material for 2D Style Rendering This section describes the newly added cartoon effect material type that converts 3D virtual models and their clothing into 2D cartoon-style visuals. - **Activation:** - Double-click the virtual model to select it. - In the Property Editor, open the Material Options tab. - Change the material type to “Cartoon Effect Only 3D.” - **Effect Options:** - **Shadow Section:** - Choose shadow color. - Adjust shadow strength to sharpen edges. - Modify flatness to control shadow range. - **Contour Line Section:** - Select contour line mode. - Adjust line width to create high-quality outlines. - **Result:** Produces stylized 2D cartoon textures on 3D models. - **Additional Resources:** For more detailed settings, refer to the CLO official website. --- ## UV Editing Support for CLO and External Virtual Models This section introduces UV editing capabilities for virtual models and costumes within CLO, enhancing texture mapping workflows. - **Starting UV Editor:** - Access the UV editor from the main menu. - In the UV editor interface, use the vertical menu bar to add UV display objects. - **UV Map Display:** - Display UV maps of the entire virtual model or selected costume parts in the 3D window. - Open the virtual model display to view all UV maps in the interface. - **Selective UV Map Viewing:** - Select specific UV display objects to isolate and view only the relevant UV maps. - This selection simplifies workflows by focusing on necessary elements, reducing clutter in complex scenes. --- # Summary CLO 2026.0 introduces significant enhancements to virtual model handling: - **Hybrid Transformation:** Real-time, slider-based body and facial expression adjustments using external 3D data (GLB/GLTF/VRM). - **Customized Configurations:** Integration with ZACS documents for easy merging of external elements based on joint name matching. - **Cartoon Effect Material:** New 2D cartoon style rendering with customizable shadow and contour line options. - **UV Editing:** Support for detailed UV map viewing and editing on both CLO and external virtual models, improving texture workflow efficiency. These features collectively improve convenience, customization flexibility, and creative expression in virtual model design within CLO.
